title: Regional Capacity Gap Mapper & Hardware Primer
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet maps current and projected regional capacity against SLA-driven demand curves to identify the incremental hardware (BOM) required to close shortfalls. Focused on Private/VPC deployments that need predictable latency SLOs and regional isolation (NA, EU, APAC).

High-level scope:
- Time horizon: next 18 months (Q2 2026 -> Q3 2027)
- Regions: us-east (NA), eu-west (EU), ap-southeast (APAC)
- Workloads: low-latency interactive chat (p95 latency target), async batch reranking, embeddings (background)
- Output: per-region GPU counts by SKU, BOM line items (nodes, networking, PSUs), lead-time risk multiplier, capital spend estimate, and three sensitivity scenarios.

Assumptions (editable):
- Target p95 latency SLO (interactive): 250ms
- Typical model served: 30B-70B class quantized variant (mixed precision / 4-bit), baseline per-GPU inference throughput (tokens/sec):
  - 40B quantized on A10x: ~450 tokens/sec (steady-state average)
  - 70B quantized on A100-like: ~650 tokens/sec
  (We treat these as configurable inputs in the sheet.)
- Average request size (tokens): 180 tokens (input+output)
- Requests per active user per minute: 3
- Regional active users growth (current -> 18 months): us-east 1.0x -> 2.2x, eu-west 1.0x -> 1.6x, ap-southeast 0.5x -> 1.4x
- Desired GPU utilization target (avg): 70% for predictability; burst headroom to 85% with autoscaling
- Safety buffer: 10% baseline + region-specific latency headroom (0–15%)
- Spare rotation policy: keep 5% warm spares on hand; procurement lead time baseline 12 weeks

Key metrics and formulas (for sheet cells):
- peak_RPS_by_region = peak_active_users_region * requests_per_user_per_min / 60
- tokens_per_sec_demand = peak_RPS * avg_request_tokens
- effective_tokens_per_sec_per_GPU = baseline_tokens_per_sec * utilization_target
- required_GPUs = ceil( tokens_per_sec_demand / effective_tokens_per_sec_per_GPU * (1 + safety_buffer) )
- BOM_nodes = ceil(required_GPUs / gpus_per_node)
- capex_estimate = sum(BOM_line_unit_cost * quantity)
- lead_time_risk_mult = 1 + risk_pct (risk_pct configured per region; e.g., APAC 0.18 for customs/transport)

Sample inputs (example scenario snapshot - editable in sheet):
- Current active users (DAU) baseline: us-east: 42,000; eu-west: 24,000; ap-southeast: 10,500
- Peak fraction of DAU concurrently active (peak concurrency window): 8%
- requests_per_user_per_min: 3
- avg_request_tokens: 180
- model throughput baseline used: 70B quantized -> 600 tokens/sec (conservative across fleet)
- utilization target: 70%
- safety_buffer by region: us-east 0.10, eu-west 0.12, ap-southeast 0.15
- gpus_per_node: 8 (dense 4U chassis)
- GPU SKU unit cost (capex): A100-like = $27,000, A10x-like = $14,000
- node chassis + NVMe + NIC + psu + rack cost = $18,000 per 8-GPU node (excl GPUs)

Worked example (us-east, snapshot):
- DAU: 42,000; peak concurrency = 0.08 -> peak_active_users = 3,360
- peak_RPS = 3,360 * (3 / 60) = 168 RPS
- tokens_per_sec_demand = 168 * 180 = 30,240 tps
- effective_tokens_per_sec_per_GPU = 600 * 0.70 = 420 tps/GPU
- required_GPUs_raw = 30,240 / 420 = 72.0 -> required_GPUs = ceil(72 * (1 + 0.10 safety)) = ceil(79.2) = 80 GPUs
- nodes_needed = ceil(80 / 8) = 10 nodes
- GPU_capex = 80 * 27,000 = $2,160,000
- Node_infra_capex = 10 * 18,000 = $180,000
- subtotal_capex = $2,340,000
- lead_time_risk_mult (us-east conservative) = 1.08 -> procurement_target_budget = $2,527,200

BOM table (text representation for sheet tab 'BOM'):
| line_item | unit | qty (us-east) | unit_cost | total |
| GPUs (A100-like) | each | 80 | 27000 | 2,160,000 |
| Nodes (8-GPU chassis) | each | 10 | 18000 | 180,000 |
| Top-of-Rack switches (100GbE) | each | 2 | 12,000 | 24,000 |
| Power distribution & UPS share | lot | 1 | 35,000 | 35,000 |
| Rack & rail, installation | per-rack | 2 | 6,000 | 12,000 |
| Spare GPUs (5%) | each | 4 | 27000 | 108,000 |
| Other (cables, test kit) | lot | 1 | 8,000 | 8,000 |
| subtotal | | | | 2,527,000 |
(rounded to procurement target above)

Regional summary quick table (example outputs):
- us-east: GPUs 80 (10 nodes), procurement target $2.53M, lead time 12 wks, lead_time_risk_mult 1.08
- eu-west: GPUs 46 (6 nodes -> 48 provisioned), procurement target approx $1.52M, lead time 14 wks (EU customs / VAT), risk_mult 1.12
- ap-southeast: GPUs 36 (5 nodes -> 40 provisioned), procurement target approx $1.35M, lead time 18 wks, risk_mult 1.18

Sensitivity scenarios (sheet tabs: S1_conservative, S2_base, S3_aggressive):
- S1 (conservative): lower growth, utilization target 60%, safety buffer +15% -> increases nodes by ~1.25x vs base
- S2 (base): numbers above
- S3 (aggressive): assume model quantization improvements +30% throughput -> effective_tokens_per_sec_per_GPU increases and required GPUs drop ~25%

Procurement & ops notes (working checklist):
- Confirm SKU qualification matrix with serving-runtime (ticket: JIRA-PRJ-4982)
- Validate node chassis thermal envelope at target rack density (SRE signoff)
- Schedule 3rd-party logistics for APAC shipments; factor in customs hold days
- Reserve vendor lead times in procurement system; set auto-trigger when utilization > 80% consistently for 2 weeks
- Define burn-down plan for old generation GPUs (decomm + remarket) to fund partial refresh

Failure modes & mitigation (notes-to-self):
- If per-GPU throughput underperforms: add hot-swap capacity on dedicated warm pool, temporarily route lower-priority requests to Hosted API routing.
- If lead time slips: re-route certain workloads to neighboring region and enable cross-region KV cache priming.
- If spotty network fabric reduces effective throughput: reduce per-node density, increase NIC count, or shift to higher-clock SKU.

Open questions for next sync (owner in parentheses):
- Confirm exact per-model tokens/sec baselines from runtime perf lab for quantized 70B (Marco)
- Decide whether to overprovision by full 1 node per region vs rely on cross-region burst (Leah)
- Estimate customs VAT and import duty exposure per APAC country (Finance / Ops)

Appendix: quick formula references and cell mapping (sheet uses named ranges):
- NAMED_RANGE: peak_RPS_{region} -> cell B3 on tab 'demand_inputs'
- NAMED_RANGE: model_tps -> cell C4 on tab 'perf_refs'
- NAMED_RANGE: safety_buffer_{region} -> tab 'demand_inputs' col E

Notes: this is a working artifact intended to be iterated in weekly capacity review. Keep the numeric cells editable and clearly labeled; keep narrative notes in the top sheet.
